text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

The panel composition doesn't help you here: you are a man, the appointee is a man, and you were shortlisted. There is no plausible mechanism by which anti-male bias produced this outcome. An all-male panel may say something about the school's gender balance generally, but raising it would weaken your case by looking scattershot.

Your actual grievance is stronger and simpler: on the stated criteria you appear better qualified — a master's in educational leadership and five years as deputy principal versus unspecified "courses." That is a merit and process argument.

Focus on the unanswered request for written reasons. Send a formal follow-up citing your right to a reasoned decision, then escalate to the appointing authority or an ombudsman if needed.
